body.purpose: Ordinary product text and authored study prose.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single action that advances the current task.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--accent, #c24a2b); color: var(--canvas, #fafafa); font: 500 0.8125rem/1.4 'Inter Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 180ms ease, border-color 180ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--accent, #c24a2b) 88%, black); } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--accent, #c24a2b) 80%, black); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Quiet Button
components.description: A reversible tool, toggle, or secondary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-quiet { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--raised, #fff); color: var(--ink, #0f1115); font: 500 0.8125rem/1.4 'Inter Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; transition: background 180ms ease, border-color 180ms ease; } .ds-btn-quiet:hover { border-color: var(--muted, #5e6470); background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--rule, #e5e7eb) 38%, var(--canvas, #fafafa)); } .ds-btn-quiet:active { background: var(--accent-quiet, #f8e9e4); } .ds-btn-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Text Action
components.description: A low-emphasis local action inside an adequately sized hit region.
components.css: .ds-text-action { min-height: 44px; padding: 0 4px; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--muted, #5e6470); font: 500 0.8125rem/1.4 'Inter Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 3px; } .ds-text-action:hover { color: var(--ink, #0f1115); } .ds-text-action:active { color: var(--accent, #c24a2b); } .ds-text-action:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 3px; }

components.name: Ruled Book Row
components.description: The signature continuous scanning row for a library book.
components.css: .ds-book-row { width: 100%; min-height: 76px; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 42px minmax(0, 1fr) auto; gap: 14px; align-items: center; padding: 14px 8px; border: 0; border-block-end: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb); border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #0f1115); text-align: left; } .ds-book-row:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--rule, #e5e7eb) 40%, transparent); } .ds-book-row:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-book-cover { width: 38px; aspect-ratio: 2 / 3; background: var(--accent, #c24a2b); border-radius: 2px; } .ds-book-copy { display: grid; gap: 4px; min-width: 0; font: 400 0.8125rem/1.4 'Inter Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-book-copy strong { overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; font: 600 1.125rem/1.3 'Source Serif 4 Variable', Georgia, serif; } .ds-book-copy span, .ds-book-progress { color: var(--muted, #5e6470); font: 400 0.6875rem/1.4 'Inter Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Reader Toolbar
components.description: Compact reader identity and quiet access to complete adjacent surfaces.
components.css: .ds-reader-toolbar { min-height: 52px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding: 4px 10px; border-block-end: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb); background: var(--canvas, #fafafa); color: var(--ink, #0f1115); font: 500 0.8125rem/1.4 'Inter Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-reader-toolbar strong { font: 600 1.125rem/1.3 'Source Serif 4 Variable', Georgia, serif; } .ds-reader-toolbar span { min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; color: var(--muted, #5e6470); } .ds-reader-toolbar div { min-width: 0; margin-inline-start: auto; display: flex; overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: none; } .ds-reader-toolbar div::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none; } .ds-reader-toolbar button { min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: inherit; font: inherit; } .ds-reader-toolbar button:hover { background: var(--accent-quiet, #f8e9e4); } .ds-reader-toolbar button[aria-pressed='true'] { color: var(--accent, #c24a2b); background: var(--accent-quiet, #f8e9e4); } .ds-reader-toolbar button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Reader Panel
components.description: One header and one scroll body for Contents, Text, or Study.
components.html:
Contents

components.css: .ds-reader-panel { width: min(320px, 100%); min-height: 240px; border-inline-start: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb); background: var(--canvas, #fafafa); color: var(--ink, #0f1115); font: 400 0.8125rem/1.5 'Inter Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-reader-panel header { min-height: 52px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 4px 14px; border-block-end: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb); } .ds-reader-panel header button { width: 44px; height: 44px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: inherit; font-size: 1.25rem; } .ds-reader-panel header button:hover { background: var(--accent-quiet, #f8e9e4); } .ds-reader-panel header button:focus-visible, .ds-reader-panel a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-reader-panel div { display: grid; padding: 10px 14px; } .ds-reader-panel a { padding: 10px 0; border-block-end: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb); color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-reader-panel a:hover { color: var(--accent, #c24a2b); }

components.css: .ds-study-lesson { max-width: 48rem; margin-inline: auto; padding: 8px 0 24px; border-block-end: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb); color: var(--ink, #0f1115); } .ds-study-lesson > header { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between; gap: 20px; margin-block-end: 22px; } .ds-study-lesson small { color: var(--muted, #5e6470); font: 500 0.6875rem/1.4 'Inter Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-study-lesson h3 { max-width: 24ch; margin: 3px 0 0; font: 600 clamp(1.5rem, 1.15rem + 0.9vw, 2rem)/1.12 'Source Serif 4 Variable', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: -0.02em; } .ds-study-lesson button { min-height: 44px; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--muted, #5e6470); text-decoration: underline; } .ds-study-lesson > section { padding-block: 15px; font: 400 1rem/1.6 'Source Serif 4 Variable', Georgia, serif; } .ds-study-lesson > section + section { border-block-start: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--rule, #e5e7eb) 70%, transparent); } .ds-study-lesson blockquote { margin: 0; } .ds-study-question { margin-block-start: 6px; padding: 18px !important; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb) !important; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--raised, #fff); } .ds-study-lesson:focus-within { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Search Result Row
components.description: One book passage in the Search panel: a micro-label section title over a serif excerpt clamped to four lines. Ruled, never carded.
components.css: .ds-results { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; display: grid; gap: 0; } .ds-results li + li { border-top: 1px solid var(--rule, #e5e7eb); } .ds-result { width: 100%; min-height: 44px; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #0f1115); padding: 0.9rem 0; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; font: inherit; } .ds-result span { display: block; margin-bottom: 0.35rem; color: var(--muted, #5e6470); font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 700; font-family: Inter Variable, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-result q { display: -webkit-box; overflow: hidden; font-family: Source Serif 4 Variable, Iowan Old Style, Georgia, serif; line-height: 1.5; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; -webkit-line-clamp: 4; } .ds-result:hover { color: var(--accent, #c24a2b); } .ds-result:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #c24a2b); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
Bookhand begins as a quiet private library, not a dashboard. The interface recedes while a person reads, then becomes an active place of study when the reader asks for it. Its warmth comes from real book artwork, literary type, and one restrained accent rather than beige product chrome, decorative texture, or nostalgia pasted onto controls.

The default world is calm, precise, quietly warm, and flat by default. Fine rules, compact typography, honest state changes, and clear spatial transitions carry hierarchy. The Study surface may become richer and more expressive than the library, but it remains a composed learning artifact rather than a chat transcript or a grid of equally weighted records.

This system is also an embedded design prompt. It describes how the shipped world achieves harmony so people and agents can create different coherent worlds. The default palette and components are reference-quality starting points, not a restriction on customization.
keyCharacteristics: Reader-first, with chrome that yields to the book.
Ruled and typographic rather than card-based.
One rare accent voice, used for meaning rather than decoration.
Complete theme worlds, not an EPUB rectangle inside unrelated chrome.
User-controlled customization with preview, reset, and Undo where persistent.
Native study artifacts that remain visibly grounded in their sources.

rules.name: The Whole-World Theme Rule
rules.body: A reading theme changes every visible reader surface: EPUB, chrome, panels, controls, overlays, focus, Study artifacts, and status UI. Never leave a bright application frame around a dark book or apply a new accent without checking it against every surface it touches.

rules.name: The One Accent Voice Rule
rules.body: A customized world may replace Terracotta Spine with any deliberate accent, but ordinary chrome should still speak with one primary accent occupying roughly ten percent or less of the surface. Additional highlight colors label user meaning; they do not become competing brand colors.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Keep one literary voice and one operational voice. Custom typography may replace either family, but must preserve the role contrast and cannot leak application type rules into publisher content.

rules.name: The Borrowed Voice Rule
rules.body: Book words keep the literary voice even when they appear inside product chrome. A search result's excerpt, a quoted highlight, and a study quotation are set in the serif because they are the book speaking; the label above them stays operational. Never set the book's own words in the product font merely because they are inside a panel.

rules.name: The Book Gets the Space Rule
rules.body: Reader chrome and diagnostics must justify every permanent pixel. Navigation can overlay or recede on mobile; it must not reserve broad rails that make the book feel like a preview.

rules.name: The Structural Depth Rule
rules.body: Prefer a rule, tonal change, or spatial move to a shadow. Shadows appear only when an element temporarily floats above reading content; never combine broad soft shadows with ornamental borders.

rules.name: The Rounder Means Louder Rule
rules.body: The eight-pixel radius is reserved for blocks that interrupt: something happened that the person did not do, or a change did not land. Ordinary content never earns it. If a new surface wants the softer corner, ask whether it is actually interrupting, and if not, give it the control radius.

rules.name: The Diagnostics Are Not Study Rule
rules.body: Raw agent telemetry — tool names, call lists, counts, success and failure history — never appears in Study. Study is the learner's material; a scrolling log of what a model did is a different surface with a different audience, and putting it in the study viewport tells the learner the machinery matters as much as the lesson. The only agent-facing element Study may carry is a compact semantic status for guidance happening right now, saying what is being explained and exposing Back and Stop. This is an invariant. Observability must remain a separate diagnostics surface.

dos: **Do** treat the shipped themes as excellent examples of a semantic system, not as the only palettes Bookhand may support.
**Do** define a complete token world before applying an agent-authored theme.
**Do** preserve hierarchy, contrast, source grounding, user control, and a visible reset path when experimenting boldly.
**Do** inspect customization on library, reader, panels, Study, mobile, desktop, error, focus, and reduced-motion states.
**Do** let the artifact dominate Study and keep tool history in separate diagnostics.
**Do** state background work honestly where it happens: name the readiness of a slow index in one calm live-region line, and keep the person's Pause and Resume visible the whole time it runs.
**Do** use real book content and real product state in demonstrations.
donts: **Don't** turn Bookhand into a generic dashboard, chat transcript, card grid, fake bookshelf, or collection of equally weighted controls.
**Don't** equate “bookish” with beige application chrome, parchment texture, paper grain, ornamental shadows, or nostalgic decoration.
**Don't** apply dark or sepia only inside the EPUB while leaving the shell in another world.
**Don't** let custom CSS, model text, diagrams, or labs escape their bounded rendering surfaces or silently rewrite publisher content.
**Don't** hard-code the current terracotta palette into new study primitives; consume semantic tokens so user-created worlds remain coherent.
**Don't** preserve a weak customization merely because an agent created it; preview, validate, revise, and keep Reset or Undo visible.

**Don't** mark identity with a logo badge floating in a corner. Bookhand is named by the wordmark in the masthead and by the book artwork itself; a badge is product chrome asserting itself in an interface whose whole intent is to recede.
